newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bund vol digs in ahead of G7.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bund vol digs in ahead of G7.

text.p: Implied volatilty of Bund options traded on LIFFE was held firm on Friday by a combination of strong German data and the prospect of the G7 meeting, traders said.
Although trade was generally slack and there were no major U.S. figures to focus the market, traders said they were reluctant to sell volatility short ahead of the weekend.
"Volume isn't great but there is no let up in the feeling of consternation," said one local trader. "You'd be a fool to sell the vol down."
August options volatility on the September Bund future was at 5.43 percent versus 5.4 percent at the open. September was steady at 5.44 percent and December little moved at 5.51 percent.
July serial options expire on Monday.
September futures were up 20 basis points at 101.17 at 1005 GMT.
Earlier German May M3 data came in stronger than expected showing annualised growth of 7.0 percent versus the final quarter of 1996, against an expected 6.4 percent rate.
The Bundesbank said growth accelerated in May because of stronger lending in the private sector. However the market quickly shrugged off the surprise and reversed much of the losses.
"It was a bit of a shock but futures recovered quickly and the vol didn't show much of a movement," said a European bank trader.
He said the usual Friday sell off in volatility was likely to be less marked than normal as the G7 summmit in Denver gets under way later today.
Activity in Bund options was dominated by a combo in September. The 3,000 lot trade involved selling the 99.00 strike puts and buying the 102.00 strike calls.
